memo: No clause diverges from the playbook. Section 3 (Term) and Section 4 (Governing Law) match the standard positions. This agreement can be signed as drafted.

- Section 4 (Liability): HIGH. The cap of one month of fees is far below the playbook minimum of twelve months. Ask for twelve months.
- Section 3 (Term and Renewal): MEDIUM. The agreement renews automatically and needs 120 days notice to cancel. The playbook allows 60 days at most.
- Section 2 (Fees): LOW. Payment is due in 15 days. The playbook standard is 30 days.

- Section 3 (Fees): LOW. Payment terms match the playbook, noted for completeness.
No other clause diverges. Section 4 (Insurance) meets the playbook minimum.

- Section 2 (Fees): MEDIUM. Fees rise 8 percent a year. The playbook caps increases at 3 percent.
- Section 3 (Assignment): MEDIUM. The vendor can assign without consent. The playbook requires consent.
- Section 9 (Insurance): LOW. The insurance clause is weaker than the playbook.

- Section 4 (Repairs): HIGH. The tenant carries all structural repairs. The playbook leaves structural repairs with the landlord.
- Section 7 (Appendix A: Rules): MEDIUM. The landlord can change the rules at any time and a breach is a default.
- Section 3 (Operating Costs): MEDIUM. There is no annual cap on the tenant's share.
- Section 6 (Assignment): MEDIUM. Consent to assign may be withheld for any reason, notwithstanding anything to the contrary herein.

- Section 2 (Fees): LOW. Payment terms may be a concern for cash flow.
- Section 3 (Data): HIGH. The vendor may keep and reuse camera footage. The playbook forbids reuse.
